newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Russia's Chernomyrdin arrives in Ukraine for talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Chernomyrdin arrives in Ukraine for talks.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin arrived in the Ukrainian capital on Wednesday to pave the way for President Boris Yeltsin to sign a much-delayed friendship treaty on May 31.
"There's work to be done," was all Chernomyrdin said as he rushed past a crowd of reporters after arrival.
Chernomyrdin was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying before his departure from Moscow that he was hopeful a treaty would be signed this week with President Leonid Kuchma.

"Most of the document's clauses have been agreed and I hope to get everything ready so the Russian president's first official visit to Kiev will take place and a deal with Ukraine will be signed," Chernomyrdin was quoted as saying.
Yeltsin has postponed a visit to Kiev to sign a post-Soviet treaty six times since Ukraine became independent from the Soviet Union in 1991.
The key sticking point has been the division and stationing of the Black Sea Fleet, based at the port of Sevastopol on the Crimean peninsula which Moscow transferred to Ukraine from Russia in 1954.

Russia had insisted that Ukraine base its share of the ships 140 km (90 miles) north of Sevastopol, but sources close to the talks in Sevastopol said this week that the two sides had agreed to moor their vessels at different bays at the city.

In Kiev, a foreign ministry official said Chernomyrdin and Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko would sign three documents -- one setting terms for basing Russian ships in Ukraine, the second dividing the fleet and the third spelling out what Moscow would pay Kiev for rent.
The two premiers would also sign economic cooperation deals and the presidents would sign the overall friendship treaty and a statement on Sevastopol as well as other documents, he said.
